text: You've been there: endless buffering, pixelated calls, pages that just won't load. Your internet feels painfully slow, and all you want is for things to *work*.
So you check plans. There's a cheap one, then a mid-tier, then super-fast. Your eye goes to the lowest price, but then you notice its speed.
Why is that cheapest option so terrible? It's barely functional, making you wonder why it even exists. Who actually uses that plan, right?
This isn't an accident. Providers intentionally design the slowest tier to be just frustrating enough to make the *next* plan up look like an incredible value.
The cost isn't just money; it's the psychological push. The 'bad' cheapest option makes the 'good' middle option seem essential, not just an upgrade.
So next time you're choosing, you'll see past the advertised speeds. You'll understand the slowest plan exists to sell you something faster.
